summary:
LunarLandingAI is an intelligent lunar landing site analysis system designed to evaluate environmental conditions and communication visibility near the Moon's South Pole.

The project combines NASA lunar elevation data, solar and Earth ephemerides, and terrain geometry to determine how surrounding topography affects sunlight exposure and direct line of sight to Earth.

By analyzing terrain obstruction, solar elevation, and Earth visibility over time, the system helps identify potential landing locations that offer better lighting conditions and communication opportunities.

This project addresses an important challenge in lunar exploration: selecting safe and operationally suitable landing sites in the Moon's polar regions, where extreme terrain and lighting conditions can significantly affect mission operations.

Our goal is to support more informed lunar landing site selection through data-driven scientific analysis.
details:
LunarLandingAI is a Python-based scientific analysis system developed to evaluate potential lunar landing sites, with an initial focus on the Moon's South Pole.

The system integrates several types of scientific data and computational models to investigate the relationship between lunar terrain, solar illumination, and communication visibility with Earth.

How It Works:

  1. Lunar Terrain Analysis:
    The system processes NASA Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) Digital Elevation Model data to extract surface elevations and analyze the surrounding terrain. A terrain horizon engine evaluates 360 azimuth directions around the observation point, using a maximum analysis range of 50 kilometers.
  2. Solar Geometry and Illumination:
    NASA JPL Horizons ephemerides are used to obtain the Sun's azimuth and elevation over time. These observations are combined with terrain horizon calculations to determine whether the solar disk is visible, partially visible, or obstructed by surrounding terrain.
  3. Earth Visibility and Communication Geometry:
    The system calculates Earth's apparent direction from the lunar observation site and evaluates terrain obstruction to determine whether direct geometric line of sight is available.
  4. SPICE Integration:
    NASA NAIF SPICE Toolkit and SpiceyPy are integrated to support independent astronomical geometry calculations and reference-frame validation.
  5. Data Validation and Results:
    The system generates structured CSV datasets, JSON summaries, and validation reports. Its initial validation pipeline successfully passed 10 out of 10 data and geometry checks. Reference-frame validation also passed 16 checks, with three remaining cautions requiring further investigation.

Technology Used:

  • Programming Language: Python.
  • Geospatial Processing: Rasterio, NumPy.
  • Astronomy and Orbital Geometry: NASA JPL Horizons, NAIF SPICE Toolkit, SpiceyPy.
  • Terrain Data: LOLA Digital Elevation Models.
  • Data Processing: Pandas and CSV/JSON.
  • Development Environment: Python virtual environment and Windows.

Current Project Results:

The initial South Pole test location was analyzed using 49 hourly observations covering November 15–17, 2026.

The solar illumination engine classified all 49 observations as visible or partially visible, with no terrain-blocked observations.

The Earth visibility engine classified all 49 observations as terrain-blocked at the initial test location.

These initial results demonstrate how terrain geometry and astronomical positioning can be combined to evaluate important environmental constraints for lunar landing operations.

Project Goals:

  • Identify lunar locations with favorable solar illumination.
  • Evaluate terrain-related communication visibility with Earth.
  • Support scientific comparison of candidate landing sites.
  • Develop a scalable framework for future lunar surface mission planning.
